subject: SOC2 details & cloud carve-out clarification — Greystone Health
messages:
From: Lisa Carter <lisa.carter@greystonehealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Greystone Security Team <security@greystonehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: SOC2 evidence request + cloud provider carve-outs

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking this. Greystone is starting our formal vendor risk assessment for Redwood and we need to collect your SOC 2 Type II report (most recent period), any bridge letters covering the gap to our contract effective date, and clarity on subservice organizations / carve-outs (specifically how you treat cloud providers like AWS/GCP, and whether any controls are carved out to third-party subprocessors).

A few concrete asks:
- Please confirm the SOC 2 audit period covered (start/end dates).
- Do you issue bridge letters if the report period doesn’t fully cover our contract start (we go live 2026-04-01)? If so, what is the earliest date you can issue one and what language is typical?
- Provide a list of subservice organizations / subprocessors referenced in the report and whether they’re a carve-out or carve-in (we need this for our internal SIG/CAIQ mapping).
- Any evidence portal or secure share for attachments (we prefer a link rather than email attachments).

If it helps, we can sign an NDA for the full report access, or accept a redacted copy. Goal is to complete our risk review by 2026-03-26.

Appreciate your quick help — if you can confirm next steps today that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Lisa Carter
Director, Vendor Risk Management
Greystone Health

Short answer up front: we can provide the SOC 2 Type II report and a bridge letter; we also maintain a current subservice org/subprocessor list. I’m looping in Mina (Security Program) to provide the technical carve-out language and confirm the audit period. Rachel from Legal is cc’d for NDA / access terms if you prefer a portal link.

Immediate next steps:
- I’ll attach the most recent SOC 2 report and a draft bridge-letter template for your review.
- Mina will follow up with whether the cloud providers are carve-out or carve-in and the subprocessors list.
- If you want portal access, confirm a contact + email and Rachel will send the secure share link or the NDA.

We’ll aim to turn around any additional SIG/CAIQ work within 3 business days after we get your confirmed scope.

Attaching: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2024.pdf (redacted) — full copy available via secure portal.

Best,
Priyom Das

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Carter <lisa.carter@greystonehealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 13:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 evidence request + cloud provider carve-outs

Hi Lisa — Mina from Redwood Security here. Thanks for the detailed asks; below are answers and short explanations. Happy to jump on a 20-min call if you want to go line-by-line.

1) Audit period (SOC 2 Type II):
   - Period covered in the attached report: 2024-01-01 through 2024-12-31.
   - The report was issued on 2025-02-15 (auditor: GreenBridge LLP).

2) Bridge letter:
   - We do provide a SOC 2 bridge letter where appropriate. Typical content: confirmation of no material changes to the control environment since the end of the audit period and a statement of the current control posture. We can issue a bridge letter dated to cover up to 2026-03-31; draft attached (Redwood_SOC2_BridgeLetter_20260312.pdf).
   - Timeline: we can provide a signed bridge letter within 3 business days once the scope and recipient are confirmed.

3) Subservice organizations / carve-out treatment:
   - Primary cloud provider: Amazon Web Services (AWS). In the SOC 2 report we treat AWS as a carve-out for physical infrastructure controls (standard shared-responsibility approach).
   - For logical, application-layer controls that are performed by Redwood (e.g., model runtime access controls, key rotation managed by Redwood) those are carve-in (covered by Redwood’s controls).
   - We maintain an inventory of subprocessors/subservice orgs. The current list includes:
       • AWS (carve-out for physical/datacenter controls)
       • CloudChecks Inc. (monitoring & vulnerability scanning; carve-in — we retain responsibility for remediation)
       • DataTransit LLC (managed networking; limited carve-out for network transport)
   - I attached Subservice_Org_List_2024.xlsx which maps each subservice org to control domains (security, availability, confidentiality). If you’d like us to map those rows to SIG/CAIQ control IDs we can do that as a follow-up.

4) Evidence portal / secure share:
   - We prefer to use our secure evidence share for full reports and attachments. Link: https://drive.google.com/redwood-evidence/greystone-portal.
   - If you require an NDA prior to portal access, please indicate the contact for signature. Legal (Rachel) can send the portal invite once NDA is in place.

5) SIG/CAIQ / questionnaire work: we can pre-fill parts of the CAIQ or SIG baseline within 3 business days for typical enterprise scopes. For custom requests (e.g., deeper pen-test evidence) timeline may extend.

Notes and caveats: the SOC 2 report contains some redacted vendor-specific items (customer data samples). If you need un-redacted sections we’ll require a mutual NDA. The bridge letter is explicit that it does not replace a full attestation but bridges the period coverage on the auditor’s limited basis.

Attachments provided in secure portal: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2024.pdf (full/redacted per NDA), Redwood_SOC2_BridgeLetter_20260312.pdf (draft), Subservice_Org_List_2024.xlsx

If you want, Priyom and I can host a short call tomorrow to walk through the Subservice_Org_List mapping to your SIG.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference
